title: Super Heavy (Starship V3 booster)
note: SpaceX Super Heavy, Starship V3 (Block 3) booster, as first flown on Flight 12 (booster B19; SpaceX photo names), on its own without the ship. Dry, unfuelled (no frost). Frame: z up, the engine bell exits at z = 0, the axis on x = y = 0. +x is the side the ship's heat shield faces (the heat-shield-side grid fin), away from the launch tower; -x faces the tower. y completes a right-handed frame. No reference 3D model exists (see reference_model): the layout comes from the sources below and from SpaceX photos, scaled by the 9 m diameter. The ship is its own model (starship).

reference_model.note: Searched gh api repos/nasa/NASA-3D-Resources on 2026-10-28: no SpaceX vehicle. No official 3D model. NASA's 3D Resources has no Starship; the models online are third-party marketplace models, not sources.

height.quote: Super Heavy was initially 71 m (233 ft) tall (in its Block 1 and Block 2 design, now retired), while Block 3 Super Heavy is 72.3 meters tall.

also.quote: The stainless-steel booster stands 236 feet tall (72 meters) and boasts a diameter of 9 m (29.5 ft).

height.note: z extent from the lowest engine bell to the top of the hot-stage ring.

diameter.quote: boasts a diameter of 9 m (29.5 ft)

engines.quote: The fuel transfer tube, which channels cryogenic fuel from the main tank to the 33 Raptor engines, has been completely redesigned

inner_engines.quote: shielding has been added to the surface area between engines and around the thrust vector control hardware on the inner 13 engines
inner_engines.also: wiki_starship: "This system uses electric actuators on the thirteen engines in the middle and center rings."

engine_rings.source: spacex_v3, inferred, not stated: 33 engines with 13 in the centre and middle rings; 3 in the centre (nsf_block3_mars), so 10 middle and 20 outer.

centre_engine_clocking_deg.quote: Currently, the center engines are 120 degrees apart and symmetrical. Block 3 will be 108, 108, and 140 degrees apart, resulting in an unsymmetrical layout.
centre_engine_clocking_deg.note: As quoted the three gaps add to 356 degrees, not 360: 144 is what closes the circle. See open_questions.

no_engine_shrouds.quote: Large individual engine shrouds have been eliminated ... Sensors and controllers are now internally integrated and covered by engine thermal protection, eliminating the need for individual engine shrouds on both Starship and Super Heavy.

raptor_sl_nozzle_exit_m.quote: Nozzle exit diameter (in) 51.226 ... Nozzle throat to exit length (in) 60.06
raptor_sl_nozzle_exit_m.note: Raptor 1-era (2019) sea-level nozzle; nothing found for Raptor 3. 51.226 in = 1.301 m; throat to exit 60.06 in = 1.526 m.

value.layout: T: one fin on each side (+y, -y) and one on the heat-shield side (+x); none on the tower side

grid_fins.quote: spacex_v3: "The number of grid fins has been reduced from four to three, with each fin now 50% larger and significantly stronger. These fins include a new catch point and have been re-clocked on the booster ... They have also been lowered". nsf_block3_mars: "they are spaced in a T shape, with a fin on the port and starboard sides, and then one on the non-tower side or the heat shield side of the ship." wiki_starship: "three electrically actuated grid fins, in a 90/90/180 degree arrangement. Two of these fins have hardpoints"

hot_stage.value: integrated: a ring of steel struts (a crown of Vs) on top of the booster's methane tank, open between the struts
hot_stage.quote: spacex_v3: "An integrated hot stage replaces the previous single-use protective interstage. The forward dome of the booster fuel tank is now directly exposed to the Starship upper stage's Raptor engines". nsf_pad2: "topped by a nearly four-meter hot staging ring". photo_b19_lift shows the strut crown above the exposed dome.

ring_height.quote: These cylinders have a height of 1.83 m (6 ft), and a thickness of 3.97 mm (0.156 in).
ring_height.note: Weld lines every 1.83 m show on the steel in every photo: a texture detail, not geometry.

scale.source: photo_pad_f13: ship and booster both 80.5 px wide (9 m). Along the axis the photo reads short against the ascent photo (ship 47.7 m vs 52.6 m), so it seems squashed vertically: lengths there are scaled by the 52.1 m ship (0.122 m/px), widths by the diameter (0.1118 m/px). The hot-stage ring then measures 3.8 m, matching nsf_pad2's 'nearly four-meter' ring.

engines_below_skirt.source: photo_f12_ascent (Desktop_3): the bells reach about 11 px below the aft end of the booster, whose width there is about 42 px (9 m). Estimated.

nozzle_exit.source: faa_plume, fitted, not measured: 20 outer bells of faa_plume's 1.30 m don't fit around a 9 m body (circumference at the bells' centres about 24.5 m, so at most 1.22 m each). Raptor 3's nozzle isn't published; 1.2 m for every booster engine, outer ring centres at r 3.9, middle (10) at r 2.4, centre (3) at r 0.85. Ring clocking estimated.

source: photo_pad_f13 (lower-booster crop x 1244-1448, y 706-1151 of the 2600 px photo; the 9 m body is about 80 px across): box-section fairings, not thin fins: one faces the camera about 0.42 of the half-width left of centre and about 1.0 m wide, others stand out about 0.9 m past both edges. The grid fins place the camera about 30 degrees toward -y from the windward fin (the near fin sits about 0.5 of the half-width right of centre, the left fin at the left edge, the right one at the right edge and lower, so on the far side). Four fairings 90 degrees apart fit all three: -55, 35, 125 (hidden) and -145 degrees. Top 28 m kept from the earlier estimate: photo_pad_f13: strakes on both sides of the lower booster from y 885 (left) and 945 (right) down past the mount top (y 1140), standing out about 8 px (0.9 m); photo_f12_ascent shows one from about 31 m above the aft end. Estimated: 28 m for both.
render_b3_booster shows the same: three in view, about 1.1 m wide and out, tops chamfered over about 1.5 m, about 26 m above the aft end.

raceway.source: photo_pad_f13 (same crop as from_photos.chines): a line of pipe clamps the full length of the booster about 0.63 of the half-width right of centre, so 39 degrees from the camera's azimuth (-30, see from_photos.chines): 9 degrees, just under the windward fin as photo_b19_transport shows. (Earlier read as 17 degrees toward -y: that line was the edge of the fairing facing the camera.) Shape from photo_b19_transport (raceway crop x 6385-7112, y 2263-4526; the 9 m body is 2667 px across, 0.0034 m/px, and the 1.83 m rings measure 1.88 m along it): below its top the raceway is about 45 px (0.25 m) wide; at the top it swells into a fairing about 110 px (0.6 m) wide and 5.6 m long, its pointed top 1.36 m long, just under the heat-shield-side grid fin (the photo looks up from below, so heights scaled from it are unreliable: the tip is placed 0.1 m under the fin's bottom, grid_fin), tapering into the raceway over 0.5 m. Two pipes run beside it, 0.14 and 0.22 m across, about 0.6 and 1.0 m round from it (on the far side from the camera: 7.9 and 12.2 degrees), on clamps about every 1.8 m; both bend into the tank just under the fin, the wider one through a port. The pipes run on past the bottom of the photo; built down the raceway's whole length (assumed). Pipe stand-off estimated. The width 0.5 m estimated earlier from the pad photo was the raceway with its pipes.

also.quote: the fairing, pipes and clamps measured as the source above says

band.source: photo_pad_f13: a ribbed band round the booster at y 760-772 (28.2 to 29.6 m below the ring top at 0.122 m/px); photo_f12_ascent shows it dark, about 0.37 of the booster's length from the top (26.8 m). Estimated: 28 m, 1.5 m tall.

hot_stage_ring_height.source: photo_pad_f13: from the ship's base (y 529) to the bottom of the strut crown (about y 560), 31 px. Agrees with nsf_pad2's "nearly four-meter hot staging ring". Used as a cross-check only: the build takes the crown's height from hot_stage_crown.

hot_stage_struts.source: photo_b19_lift (crop 700-1220 x 170-520 of the 1600 px view): 9 strut feet across the visible half, so about 18 around; the top ring sits on the strut tops; the methane dome rises about 2.2 m above the tank's top edge (100 px below the ring top on a 680 px / 9 m body). Estimated. Strut diameter revised: photo_b19_lift (crown crop x 6062-8270, y 1299-2598 of the 12125 px photo, viewed at 0.00683 m/px: the 9 m body is 1330 px across) shows the struts about 28 px (0.19 m) across mid-length. Dome height revised: in the crown crop the dome's top is 222 px (1.52 m) below the ring's top, so 3.27 - 1.52 = 1.75 m above its base.

grid_fin.source: photo_pad_f13_close: the side fins stand out about 105 px from a 230 px (9 m) body and are about 30 px thick; photo_pad_f13: the fins' tops are about 51 px below the top of the hot-stage ring. Estimated: the close photo looks up from below, so expect a few percent of error. Shape: a grid of cells in a flat box, wider than it stands out, its outer edge serrated (photo_b19_lift). Width along the circumference: the heat-shield-side fin in photo_pad_f13_close is about 100 px wide on the 230 px body, 3.9 m. photo_b19_lift shows both side fins at the same height, about 5.8 m below the top (pad photo 6.2 m). Lattice: photo_b19_lift shows the fins' edges serrated, about 11 teeth along 342 px of a 680 px (9 m) body, so a tooth every 0.41 m; with walls at +-45 degrees, teeth fall every pitch/sqrt2 along an edge, so a wall spacing of 0.57 m. The teeth are cut about 0.35 m deep on the bottom edge; the top edge looks straight in the photo, so it isn't notched. Wall thickness 0.05 m estimated.

weld_lines.source: photo_wdr: the weld lines between the 1.83 m steel rings show in every photo but are under a pixel wide; line width (20 mm) and how dark (0.8 as bright as the steel) estimated. photo_b19_transport shows neighbouring rings differing slightly in brightness (each rolled from its own sheet): each ring's brightness is varied by up to 4%, over a 7-ring repeat (estimated).

hot_stage_crown.source: photo_b19_lift (crown crop x 6062-8270, y 1299-2598 of the 12125 px photo, viewed at 0.00683 m/px: the 9 m body is 1330 px across): the top ring is a flat band about 30 px (0.2 m) tall; the struts are round tubes tapering over about 60 px (0.4 m) at the top and 80 px (0.55 m) at the bottom to about 12 px (0.08 m); each pair's feet meet at the tank's top edge in a bracket about 50 px (0.34 m) wide and 130 px (0.9 m) tall: most are dark forks, some steel boxes on a gold base. The camera looks from the tower side (the two side fins are at the limbs, the windward fin hidden), so the crop's centre is 180 degrees; the steel boxes are at about 120, 200 and 220 degrees, the visible forks at 140, 160, 180, 240 and 260. The far side isn't seen: built with forks. Ring thickness and bracket depth estimated. Height from the dome's base (where the strut feet meet, crop y 490) to the ring's top (y 40): 450 px, 3.07 m, plus the 0.2 m ring: 3.27 m. The pad photo's 3.8 m (hot_stage_ring_height) runs to the bottom of the crown, the brackets included, and agrees within its resolution.

crown_ports.source: photo_b19_lift (crown crop x 6062-8270, y 1299-2598 of the 12125 px photo, viewed at 0.00683 m/px: the 9 m body is 1330 px across): three round ports, each in an octagonal plate about 120 px (0.82 m) across with a 50 px (0.34 m) port, 245 px (1.67 m) below the tank's top edge, at crop x 265, 895 and 1250 (body axis x 705, half-width 665 px): 139, 197 and 235 degrees. The far side isn't seen.

grid_fin_mount.source: photo_b19_lift (fin crop x 5542-9180, y 2598-3810, 0.0113 m/px): each fin turns on a round geared mount on the body at its root, about 80 px (0.9 m) across. How far it stands out estimated.

exit_diameter.source: faa_plume, fitted, not measured: see from_photos.nozzle_exit

wall.source: render_aft_b3_booster, design value: a thin wall at the lip

diameter.source: render_aft_b3_booster, scaled by the 1.2 m nozzle exit (from_photos.nozzle_exit) on the second middle-ring engine from the left: exit about 77 px wide in the 1400 px view. Widths only; heights are foreshortened (the camera looks up). Estimated. Chamber stack about 85 px wide in a 3x crop of 230 px exit.

convergent_length.source: render_aft_b3_booster, design value: the throat-to-chamber blend is hidden by plumbing

length.source: render_aft_b3_booster, design value: the chamber's ribbed stack, its height foreshortened

diameter.source: render_aft_b3_booster, scaled by the 1.2 m nozzle exit (from_photos.nozzle_exit) on the second middle-ring engine from the left: exit about 77 px wide in the 1400 px view. Widths only; heights are foreshortened (the camera looks up). Estimated. Powerhead about 75 px in the same crop.

height.source: wiki_raptor: engine "Length 3.1 m", less the nozzle (1.526), convergent (0.2) and chamber (0.35)

engine.source: faa_plume and render_aft_b3_booster: A stand-in for the booster's sea-level Raptor 3 until it is modelled as an engine of its own: the nozzle from faa_plume's Raptor table (Raptor 1-era, nothing published for Raptor 3) with the exit fitted, the rest estimated from render_aft_b3_booster. Built at lod "low" (33 engines).

aft_manifold.source: render_aft_b3_booster: a bundle of five tubes round the aft end, about 20 px tall (0.31 m) with a clamp block every ~10 degrees (about 18 across the visible half, so 36), each about 14 x 12 px; below it a dark rim about 32 px (0.5 m) tall with square holes (about 10 across the visible half, so 20). Scaled by the 1.2 m nozzle exit (77 px). Estimated.

aft_plate.source: render_aft_b3_booster: a dark plate the engines hang from, no heavy heat shield (caption: "Move to Raptor 3 eliminates the need for heavy heatshields on the bottom of the booster"); spacex_v3 adds shielding between the engines.

stainless_steel.source: photo_wdr, the leeward side of the ship's nose in daylight (native px about 2640, 820; 20 x 20 px averaged). The steel mostly mirrors its surroundings, so the colour is only a base; other samples were blue from the sky.

grid_fin.source: photo_b19_lift and photo_pad_f13: the fins are near-black like the tiles; not sampled separately.

bracket_gold.source: photo_b19_lift, the gold base of the steel strut bracket at about 200 degrees (crown crop 900, 607; 9 x 9 px). One spot; the other samples there were tinted by the sky.

open_questions: Does the 72.3 m booster height include the engine bells below the aft skirt? Not stated. Proposed: yes (overall height), so z = 0 is the bottom of the nozzles.
Booster engine rings (3 / 10 / 20) are inferred, and the centre clocking as quoted (108, 108, 140) adds to 356 degrees. This only shows from below. Proposed: 3 / 10 / 20, centre gaps 108 / 108 / 144.

Grid fins: no size in metres anywhere; photos give about 4.0 x 4.0 x 1.2 m. The two side fins are level in photo_b19_lift; whether the heat-shield fin is higher isn't clear (two photos disagree, both with strong perspective). Built level.
Hot-stage struts: 18 V pairs estimated from the visible half of photo_b19_lift.
Photos: SpaceX's licence for these isn't stated (their Flickr photos have been CC BY-NC 2.0). They stay out of the repo; the spec links them.

Not modelled: frost (only when fuelled), the tower and its chopsticks, small fittings, the booster quick-disconnect (no photo of it found: in the static-fire photo the base sits inside the launch mount).

Lower-body fairings: four, 90 degrees apart, is inferred from three in view in photo_pad_f13 and render_b3_booster. In photo_pad_f13 the one on the left edge looks about 6 m taller than the others; the render shows them level. Built level at 28 m.
